0.0.n: Short for パートタイム, commonly used for part-time jobs or workers.

0.1.n: Shows that パート is one example, not the only type of work included.

0.2.n: Marks the employment arrangement under which the women work.

0.3.n: Comes directly before 女性 to describe which women are meant.

0.4.n: Japanese nouns do not change form to show plural.

0.6.n: Combines with 手当 to name compensation paid when an employer suspends or reduces work.

0.7.n: Together with 休業, this refers to compensation for work suspended or reduced by the employer.

0.8.n: Marks 休業手当 as what people do not know about.

0.9.n: 知らぬ is a formal written negative form of 知る, equivalent here to 知らない.

0.10.n: 知らぬ directly describes this noun: people who do not know.

0.11.n: Marks the unaware people as the group whose proportion is reported.

0.12.n: 約 means approximately, and each 割 represents ten percent.

0.13.n: Marks the resulting proportion; the headline leaves out a verb such as なる.

0.15.n: Describes the survey as conducted outside government.

0.16.n: 民間調査 is a compact headline phrase identifying the source of the finding.

1.0.n: Often describes regular part-time employment, though its meaning overlaps with アルバイト.

1.1.n: Lists examples without implying that these are the only kinds of work.

1.2.n: Often used for student or side jobs, though it overlaps with パート.

1.3.n: Marks パートやアルバイト as the employment arrangement.

1.4.n: Describes 女性 directly, forming women who work in these jobs.

1.5.n: The preceding words specify the group being surveyed.

1.6.n: Links 女性 to うち to identify the group within which the proportion is measured.

1.7.n: 女性のうち narrows the statement to members of this group.

1.9.n: 禍 means calamity; コロナ禍 refers to the pandemic and its disruptive effects.

1.10.n: Marks the pandemic as the cause of reduced shifts.

1.12.n: Marks シフト as what decreased.

1.13.n: Past form of 減る, describing a reduction that occurred.

1.14.n: シフトが減った describes these people as having experienced fewer shifts.

1.15.n: Sets people with reduced shifts as the topic of the reported proportion.

1.16.n: 人 counts people; this supplies the total group size in the ratio.

1.17.n: Links the total group to the selected number in 4人に1人.

1.18.n: Completes 4人に1人, expressing one person out of every four.

1.19.n: Marks the reported result before なっている.

1.20.n: なる in the ている form presents the proportion as an established current result.

1.21.n: Introduces a contrasting finding that follows in the next line.

2.0.n: Combines with 時間 to refer to scheduled working hours.

2.1.n: Here 時間 refers to work duration, not a particular clock time.

2.2.n: Links shift hours to their shortening.

2.3.n: A noun describing a reduction in scheduled working hours.

2.4.n: Marks shortened hours as the circumstance in which payment is possible.

2.5.n: Adds emphasis: shortened hours can qualify, not just complete suspension of work.

2.6.n: Forms 休業手当 with the next word, naming compensation for employer-imposed loss of work.

2.7.n: The full term 休業手当 covers compensation that can also apply to reduced hours.

2.8.n: Marks the allowance as what can be received.

2.9.n: The potential form of 受け取る expresses possibility or eligibility here.

2.10.n: Turns the preceding statement about receiving compensation into something people may know.

2.11.n: Marks that entire fact as what people do not know.

2.12.n: Plain negative form of 知る, directly describing 人.

2.13.n: The preceding description identifies those unaware of their eligibility.

2.14.n: Marks the unaware people as the group reaching the stated proportion.

2.16.n: 割 measures tenths, so eight 割 equals eighty percent.

2.17.n: After a number, 近く expresses an amount close to that number.

2.18.n: Marks the level reached by the proportion.

2.19.n: Used with quantities to emphasize how high a figure is.

2.20.n: Turns the entire statement about the proportion into the finding revealed by the survey.

2.21.n: Marks that finding as what became clear.

2.22.n: Indicates a nongovernmental source for the survey.

2.23.n: Links 民間 to 調査, identifying who conducted the survey.

2.24.n: Refers to the investigation that produced these findings.

2.25.n: Marks the survey as the means by which the finding became known.

2.26.n: Polite past form of 分かる, used in news reports to introduce an established finding.

0.lit: Women working part-time and similar jobs: people unaware of work-suspension allowances to about eighty percent. Private-sector survey.
0.tip: Headlines often omit final verbs, as in 約8割に, leaving the result implied.

1.lit: Among women working part-time or casual jobs, people whose shifts decreased because of the pandemic stand at one-in-four, while…
1.tip: 4人に1人 means one in four; に links the total group size to the number within it.

2.lit: People unaware they can receive work-suspension allowances even for shortened shift-hours reach nearly eighty percent, a private-sector survey made clear.
2.tip: Each こと turns a preceding statement into a noun-like unit: first what people do not know, then what became clear.
